structure.title: Book I · A pin has many makers
structure.text: Smith begins inside production, where dividing tasks changes what a day of labour yields. He follows the resulting product through exchange and price into the incomes of workers, owners of stock and landlords, whose interests can diverge even when output grows.

structure.title: Books II–III · Where does the next year's work come from?
structure.text: Stock maintained and accumulated today supports future production. The inquiry then turns historical. The relationship among agriculture, towns and trade in Europe developed under institutions that often pushed investment in surprising directions.

structure.title: Book IV · Who gains when the nation is said to gain?
structure.text: Trade restrictions, colonial arrangements and rival systems of political economy receive extended trials. A merchant seeking protection can describe a private advantage as a public necessity, so Smith repeatedly asks who will pay more for the promised prosperity.

structure.title: Book V · Send the bill somewhere
structure.text: Defence, justice, roads, schools and the public debt bring government into the accounts. Different ways of paying for a bridge or a teacher can alter both access to the service and the provider's incentive to do the work well.

people.name: Division of labour
people.role: A source of output with a human cost
people.text: Specialisation increases dexterity and saves the time lost in changing tasks. Much later Smith returns to the worker whose entire day consists of a few operations, and the burden this narrowing can place on public education.

people.name: Merchants and manufacturers
people.text: Their practical knowledge makes them persuasive witnesses on proposed trade laws. The same investment that gives them knowledge can make a smaller market for competitors an attractive public policy in their eyes.

people.name: The ordinary labourer
people.role: A measure of what wealth can buy
people.text: Smith observes the tools, clothes and household goods that bring distant trades into one person's life. The labourer's purchasing power supplies a different measure of national wealth from the treasure in a government's possession.

context.title: Stock, wages, profit and rent
context.text: Stock includes resources accumulated to support or equip production. Wages, profit and rent distinguish claims on its proceeds. A rise in the price of a commodity can benefit one claimant while leaving another worse off.

context.title: Gold crossing a border
context.text: A government anxious to retain precious metals may treat their departure as a national loss. Smith asks what goods, productive capacity and opportunities for exchange actually move in return. The disagreement concerns what should go in the ledger at all.

notice.text: Follow the coats and pins beyond the workshop.
notice.why: Specialisation depends on finding buyers for output far beyond a single household's needs. A navigable river or a good road can change how finely the work inside a distant workshop can be divided.

notice.text: Ask who can wait during a wage dispute.
notice.why: Workers and employers may both be free to refuse terms. Their reserves and ability to organise can nevertheless give them very different amounts of time before refusal becomes impossible.

notice.text: Listen for the group that drafted a rule.
notice.why: Smith's account of a tariff often begins to change once the people who proposed it enter the picture. The interests of buyers dispersed across a country may have had no equally articulate voice.

opening: A pin is an insignificant object until Adam Smith looks at how it is made. Dividing the work lets a small group produce quantities no individual could approach, and that observation opens onto the wealth of entire societies. Smith follows labour, trade, prices, and government through the arrangements that fill a dinner table. He also watches merchants seek privileges and workers bear the costs of progress. The economy becomes a human construction whose remarkable productivity offers no guarantee that its rewards will be shared fairly.
